title: Cross-Border Railways (Border Control Co-location) Bill at Second Reading
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Second Minister for Home Affairs, to give effect to co-located customs, immigration and quarantine facilities and related cross-border railway arrangements for the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link.
why_it_matters: The Minister said the RTS Link is targeted to commence service this December, with peak capacity of up to 10,000 passengers per hour per direction, and will help relieve congestion on the Causeway. Under the co-located model, passengers undergo both departure and arrival immigration clearance before boarding the train and no further immigration clearance is required upon disembarkation in the other country. The Bill also sets out arrangements for cross-border incident management and concurrent criminal jurisdiction on trains in transit.

key_points.point: The Second Minister for Home Affairs moved that the Bill be now read a Second time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: I seek to move that the Bill be now read a Second time.

key_points.point: The RTS Link is targeted to commence service this December.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link (RTS Link) is targeted to commence service this December.

key_points.point: The RTS Link will have peak capacity of up to 10,000 passengers per hour per direction and is intended to relieve Causeway congestion.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: With a peak capacity of up to 10,000 passengers per hour per direction, the RTS Link will help relieve congestion on the Causeway.

key_points.point: Under the co-located CIQ model, passengers clear both departure and arrival immigration before boarding and need no further immigration clearance on disembarkation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: This allows passengers to undergo both departure and arrival immigration clearance before boarding the train, and no further immigration clearance is required upon disembarkation in the other country.

key_points.point: The Bill gives effect to arrangements on co-located CIQ facilities and coordination on railway security and cross-border incident management.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: The purpose of this Bill is to give effect to these arrangements concerning the co-location of CIQ facilities as well as the coordination between Singapore and Malaysia in railway security matters and cross-border incident management.

key_points.point: The designated areas for Malaysia remain Singapore territory and subject to Singapore's laws.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: To be clear, there is no change to territorial boundaries and the designated areas for Malaysia remain Singapore's territory and subject to Singapore's laws.

key_points.point: The Minister may withdraw recognition of any Malaysian officer at any time without providing a reason.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: clause 12 authorises the Minister to withdraw recognition of any Malaysian officer at any time without providing a reason.

key_points.point: Malaysian officers may carry restraining devices and use reasonable force to detain disorderly individuals or those posing a threat to public security.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: These include carrying restraining devices, such as batons and handcuffs when on official duty, and using reasonable force to detain disorderly individuals or those who pose a threat to public security.

key_points.point: A detained person must be transferred to an appropriate Singapore officer as soon as practicable.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: When an individual is detained, Malaysia's officers must, as soon as is practicable, transfer custody of the person to an appropriate Singapore officer.

key_points.point: Singapore officers are not allowed to make an arrest in Malaysia's territory.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: This means, for example, that Singapore officers are not allowed to make an arrest when in Malaysia's territory.

key_points.point: For cross-border incidents, where a train can complete its journey, the authorities of the country where the train stops manage the incident.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: First, where a train is able to complete its journey, any incident on board will be managed by the authorities of the country in which the train stops.

key_points.point: Both countries agreed to use the nose of the train as the marker to determine primary responsibility for an incident between Piers 47 and 48.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: both countries have agreed to use the nose of the train as the marker to determine the country with primary responsibility to manage the incident.

key_points.point: Singapore and Malaysia agreed to concurrent criminal jurisdiction over offences on board trains in transit and on the tracks between Piers 47 and 48.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: Singapore and Malaysia have agreed that both countries will have concurrent criminal jurisdiction over criminal offences that occur on board trains in transit, as well as over the stretch of railway tracks located between Piers 47 and 48.

key_points.point: For an offence on a moving train, the country where the train completes its journey has the primary right to exercise jurisdiction.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: If someone commits an offence on a moving train, what Singapore and Malaysia have agreed on is that the country where the train completes its journey will be accorded the primary right to exercise jurisdiction.

key_points.point: Data collected or generated by Singapore officers in Malaysia is treated as collected or generated in Singapore and governed by Singapore law.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: Clause 37 provides that all information and data collected or generated by Singapore officers in Malaysia in the course of official duties, whether within the designated areas or during cross-border incident management, these shall all be treated as if they were collected or generated in Singapore and governed by Singapore law.

key_points.point: Clause 43 confers immunity on Malaysian officers' actions in Singapore from Singapore's criminal, civil and administrative jurisdictions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: clause 43 confers immunity on the actions of Malaysia's officers in Singapore from Singapore's criminal, civil and administrative jurisdictions.

key_points.point: Clause 44 allows the Minister to disapply or modify provisions if protections for Singapore officers in Malaysia are substantially less favourable.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: If it is found that what Malaysia's legislation accords to our officers are substantially less favourable than what this Bill accords to their officers, clause 44 empowers the Minister to issue regulations that disapply or modify any provision of the Bill in relation to Malaysia's officers in Singapore.

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair said he supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: I support this Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asked why Malaysian law needs to apply within Singapore territory rather than relying purely on Singapore law with cooperation mechanisms.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: I think it would be helpful for the Minister to perhaps elaborate on why it is necessary for Malaysian law to have application within Singapore territory, rather than relying purely on Singapore law with the appropriate cooperation mechanisms?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asked how accountability and oversight will be ensured for actions by foreign officers in Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: Could the Minister clarify how will accountability and oversight be ensured for actions taken by foreign officers operating in Singapore?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asked whether joint patrols or onboard security personnel will be deployed on the trains.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: will joint patrols or onboard security personnel be deployed in the trains?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong said the Workers' Party supports the principles of efficiency and bilateral cooperation underpinning the Bill while seeking clarifications.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: While the Workers' Party supports the principles of efficiency and bilateral cooperation underpinning this Bill, I have several clarifications regarding legal jurisdiction, officer protection and commuter rights.

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked what physical and operational infrastructure at Woodlands North will ensure custody transfer happens immediately or as soon as practicable.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: what is the physical and operational infrastructure in place at Woodlands North to ensure this transfer happens immediately or as soon as practicable?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked for the specific public interest criteria for when Singapore would waive jurisdiction, especially if a crime is committed against a Singaporean on a Johor-bound train.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Minister whether he can clarify the specific public interest criteria used to determine when Singapore would waive the jurisdiction, especially if a crime is committed against a Singaporean on a Johor-bound train.

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked how the division of labour between SCDF and Malaysia's Bomba would be managed during a mid-track emergency.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: how will the division of labour between the SCDF and the Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia be managed and permitted under the bill during a mid-track emergency?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked whether there will be a guaranteed minimum quota of manual counters staffed by Singapore officers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: Will there be a guaranteed minimum quota of manual counters staffed by Singapore officers?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong sought confirmation that powers and functional immunity for Singaporean officers under Malaysia's RTS Link Act 2026 are substantively identical in scope to protections in this Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: I seek the Minister's confirmation that both the powers accorded and the functional immunity provided to Singaporean officers under Malaysia's RTS Link Act 2026 are substantively identical in scope to the protections we are granting under this Bill.

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng asked whether marshals or TransCom officers will be posted on board, or whether detection will rely on onboard cameras or station-based deployments.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: do we intend to post marshals or any of our Public Transport Security Command (TransCom) on board, or are we just going to depend on onboard cameras or station-based deployments to detect such incidents?

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng asked whether security deployed on board would be allowed to carry firearms and how jurisdiction would govern that.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: if we are deploying security on board, are they allowed to carry firearms?

key_points.point: Ms Sylvia Lim said the Bill to co-locate border controls should be supported.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
key_points.quote: this Bill to co-locate border controls should be supported.

key_points.point: Ms Sylvia Lim asked why the Bill does not expressly state that the country where the train journey is completed has primary jurisdiction.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
key_points.quote: Is there a reason why our Bill does not say this expressly?

key_points.point: Ms Sylvia Lim asked under what circumstances Malaysia would be obligated to cede jurisdiction to Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
key_points.quote: Under what circumstances would Malaysia be obligated to cede jurisdiction to Singapore?

key_points.point: Ms Sylvia Lim noted differences in criminal law and punishment between Singapore and Malaysia, including theft maximum sentences.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
key_points.quote: the punishment for theft in Singapore carries a maximum of three years, while in Malaysia, the maximum jail term is up to seven years.

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee said she supports the Bill and sought clarification on practical concerns for commuters.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: I support the Bill and I would like to seek clarification on several aspects of the Bill hoping to cover some of the practical concerns that commuters may have arising from the Bill.

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee noted different cash declaration thresholds under Singapore and Malaysian laws.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: where Singapore laws apply, a declaration is required if the traveller is entering or leaving Singapore with cash above S$20,000, whereas in areas where Malaysia laws apply, the threshold is US$10,000.

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee asked how the Public Prosecutor's consent mechanism will operate in practice.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: could the Minister clarify how the Public Prosecutor's consent mechanism will operate in practice?

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng said he supports the Bill because the border clearance process must be as efficient as the journey itself.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: I support this Bill because for the RTS Link to succeed, the border clearance process must be as efficient as the journey itself.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked what practical recourse a Singaporean has if they suffer harm or have their data mishandled.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: If a Singaporean suffers harm or has their data mishandled, what is their practical recourse?

key_points.point: The Minister said there are no plans to deploy enforcement officers on board the trains, but there will be comprehensive CCTV coverage monitored in real time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: There are no plans to deploy our enforcement officers on board the trains, but there will be comprehensive CCTV coverage of the interior of the train cabins that will be monitored back-end in real-time.

key_points.point: The Minister confirmed that data transmitted back to Singapore would be air-gapped.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: Mr Dennis Tan had asked whether the data that we collect, when transmitted back to Singapore, would be protected or secured and he asked whether it would be air-gapped. The answer is yes, it would be.

key_points.point: The Minister said public interest for jurisdiction is not hard-coded because each scenario depends on context and circumstances.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: We have not hard-coded what public interest might look like, because each scenario could well be different and it depends on the context, the different circumstances on which the case arises and the way in which we might view our interest in a particular offence or the individual concerned.

key_points.point: The Minister said operational agencies from both countries and the rail operator will conduct joint exercises later this year ahead of RTS Link service commencement.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: Operational agencies from both countries, along with the rail operator, will conduct joint exercises later this year, ahead of the RTS Link service commencement, both to test as well as to validate the application of these SOPs.

key_points.point: The Minister said if drugs or other illicit items are found during checks in Singapore, Singapore law applies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: Should drugs be found or, in fact, any other illicit items be found during checks done in Singapore, Singapore law would then apply.

key_points.point: The Minister said if officers at Bukit Chagar detect attempts to bring in vapes or drugs, Malaysian laws apply.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: If our officers at Bukit Chagar Station detect attempts to bring in vapes or drugs, Malaysian laws would apply.

key_points.point: The Minister said Singapore officers cannot arrest in Malaysia and Malaysian officers cannot arrest in Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: We cannot arrest in Malaysia and Malaysian officers cannot arrest in Singapore.

key_points.point: The Minister said additional deployments for serious unplanned incidents should not exceed three days in the ordinary course unless a longer duration is requested and approved.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: Such deployments should not exceed three days in the ordinary course, as provided for under paragraph 8 of the Second Schedule, unless the Malaysian Government puts in a request for a longer duration and the Minister approves this request.

key_points.point: The Minister said immunities conferred on Malaysian officers are not unconditional and depend on actions being part of official duties in designated areas.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: the immunities which the Bill confers on the actions of Malaysian officers are not unconditional.

key_points.point: The Minister said the Singapore Minister for Home Affairs can withdraw recognition of any Malaysian preclearance officer at any time without giving a reason.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: the Singapore Minister for Home Affairs has the power to withdraw recognition for any Malaysian preclearance officer at any time without giving any reason.

key_points.point: The Minister said it is unlikely anyone will be exposed to double prosecution for the same conduct as long as both sides adhere to the agreement.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: So, as long as both sides adhere to this agreement, it is unlikely that anyone will be exposed to double prosecution for the same conduct.

key_points.point: The Minister confirmed substantive reciprocity in powers and immunities for Singapore officers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: To Mr Dennis Tan's point about there being substantive reciprocity in powers and immunities, I will confirm to him that the answer is yes.

key_points.point: The Minister said the five-minute journey, CCTV coverage and real-time monitoring were reasons not to have dedicated security personnel on board by default.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: It is a five-minute journey across both ways; and with the availability of closed circuit television coverage and the real-time monitoring that will be done by the officers on both sides, we did not think that this will be necessary.

key_points.point: The Minister said there is an option to activate personnel on trains if necessary as a precaution.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
key_points.quote: there is a provision and an option to activate personnel to be on the trains, if necessary, as a precaution.

what_happens_next: The Deputy Speaker said he would put the question to the House. The Minister also said operational agencies from both countries, along with the rail operator, will conduct joint exercises later this year ahead of the RTS Link service commencement.
not_said: What specific public interest criteria will be used when deciding whether one country should waive primary jurisdiction to the other?
How will complaints about the conduct of foreign officers be investigated and resolved across jurisdictions?
Will there be a guaranteed minimum number of manual immigration counters for seniors and persons with disabilities at Woodlands North?
How will repairs, recovery or towing of a train that breaks down in transit be handled?
What protocols will apply if the two countries disagree on whether one has an obligation to cede jurisdiction?
How will differences in criminal law and punishment between Singapore and Malaysia affect cases where both countries have an interest?
Will a dedicated liaison mechanism be set up to help Singaporeans and visitors with cross-border issues?
How will data breach accountability work if the breach involves bilateral obligations or equipment in the other country?
